speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many students were subject to balloting in the 2025 Secondary 1 Posting Exercise; (b) of this number, how many were unsuccessful and consequently considered for their next choice of school despite having met the cut-off points of their higher-order choice; and (c) since 2021, how many students have been similarly unsuccessful in balloting each year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Under the Achievement Levels (AL) scoring system, more students will have identical scores.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This has been stable over the last few years.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, MOE tracks the percentage of students who were placed in a school amongst their top six choices.

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: If there is a compression of available places for non-affiliated students because Direct School Admission (DSA) for non-affiliated students do eat into the minimum quota of 20%, as we have just learnt, is this a contributing factor to student who have just met the cut-off point and nevertheless still be balloted out?

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: The second question: would MOE consider setting up a hard quota for non-affiliated and non-DSA admissions?

speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
text: So, this would ensure a meaningful and predictable number of places that remain available to students applying through the Secondary 1 admissions exercise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It varies, could be varied by one to two points, depends on each year's exercise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, in a way, each school's balloting rate depends ultimately on school choices and students' decisions, and DSA numbers and the kinds of students and numbers of students they admit each year.
